articleTitle: A microprocessor based current differential protection
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The author describes a current differential protection which is being developed on a microprocessor based modular format. The concept is to provide a flexible protection which can be built up from a standard range of modules and with suitable software can be tailored to suit a wide variety of applications from EHV power transmission down to power distribution. By suitable choice of modems, a wide range of communications media can be exploited depending on availability for a particular application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability expectations for protective relays
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors compare the reliability expectations of electromechanical and electronics-based protective relays by examining failure rate and self-test data. From such data and operational experiences, the authors suggest various guidelines for the application of electromagnetic and electronic relays to power network protection apparatus.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low impedance biased differential busbar protection for application to busbars of widely differing configuration
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Faults on busbars are rare and hence busbars are generally considered to be one of the most reliable parts of the power system. It follows, then, that any protection system applied to a busbar must be of very high integrity so as not to reduce the overall reliability. The authors describe new techniques which have been developed to eliminate the need for a stabilizing resistance and ensure thorough fault stability with a much reduced level of bias. This widens the application of the protection and also makes it suitable for retro-fit situations where it may be required to share current transformers with existing protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New development of third harmonic ground fault protection schemes for turbine-generator stator windings
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The third harmonic (150 Hz) equivalent circuit of turbine-generator stator windings is introduced. The sensitivity of various 150 Hz ground fault protection schemes for stator windings are analyzed in detail by using the equivalent circuits. A ne protection scheme with high sensitivity is deduced, whose technical characteristics have been proved in practical operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Series compensated line protection: system modelling and relay testing
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Considerable progress has been made in modelling series compensated power systems. With the introduction of computer based test benches, a method has emerged that dynamically tests line protection against a full power system model. Currents and voltages, incorporating all the electrical phenomena of series compensated lines, can be injected into relays and their responses measured within the laboratory. Using two test benches, an overall protection scheme, comprising two relays and a communication link, can be fully exercised. Beginning with a synopsis of the protection problems expected, the authors give details of a special version of distance protection for series compensated lines. The relay modifications are described, and a summary of test results given. They conclude that the advanced test procedure has given the means of testing relays for a range of difficult applications, and in particular, has proven that distance protection can be practically applied to series compensated lines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Detecting transformer winding faults using non-linear models of transformers
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors describe an algorithm that can detect winding faults in single and three phase transformers. The algorithm is suitable whether or not it is possible to measure the winding currents. The nonlinearity and hysteresis of the transformer core are considered but do not explicitly become a part of the algorithm. Therefore, B-H curve data of the transformer core are not required. A number of different operating conditions simulated on a computer were used to test the algorithm. Sample test results are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of differential protection for three-winding power transformers during transient CT's saturation
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors present the results and conclusions from extended digital simulation studies concerned with the performance of three-winding transformer differential protection under severe transient saturation of conventional current transformers (CT). The main goal of these studies was the verification of the above discrimination criterion under all possible power system conditions, having also regard to the harmonics produced by saturated CT. As a result of the investigations, some countermeasures are proposed which assure the correct fault discriminations even for extremely distorted current waveforms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Limits to zones of simultaneous tripping in multi-terminal lines
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: A technique to quantitatively determine the limits to zones of simultaneous tripping, considering the effects of various power system parameters' uncertainties, is presented. The relay reach is modelled as a function of these parameters, and mathematical programming is used to determine its optimum value, satisfying the specified set of system constraints. Simulation results are presented for different types of faults on a three-terminal line considering factors such as transmission line parameter uncertainties, metering errors, and variations in load requirements, source impedances and the charging currents.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experience and problems with the protection of series compensated lines
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors discuss the experience of Eskom in protecting series compensated lines starting with the original type 1 scheme consisting of permissive over-reaching and electromechanical impedance techniques. As more lines were constructed type 2 protection, consisting of electronic relays using sequence component operating and restraint quantities, was implemented. In 1985 a program was started to replace type 1 with type 3 protection, electronic phase and ground hybrid directional comparison protection. The main problem to be overcome, subsynchronous resonance, is also discussed. The series capacitors used in the capacitor banks and their operation are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time synchronous end-to-end relay testing
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The availability of precise time information via geo-stationary (GOES) or global positioning (GPS) satellites offers a valuable resource for synchronous control of remotely located protective relay test instruments, providing capabilities for end-to-end test of power system protection systems. The authors introduce a design for cycle-by-cycle control and synchronization of protection test instruments, illustrate a method for synchronizing and controlling protection tests instruments at remote locations using GOES/GPS satellite receivers, and suggest test methods suitable for end-to-end testing of protection systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated protection and control digital system for rural substations
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: In rural substations, various problems arise affecting the ease for exploitation and, consequently the quality of the service in the attended geographical area. The main problem is the lack of punctual information. When there is either a disconnection of an output line or a blackout due to the disconnection of the input lines in a rural substation, only the 'users calls' indicate that a problem has appeared. The authors describe an integrated protection and telecontrol system for such rural substations which overcomes these problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach to high speed relaying based on transient phenomena
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors present a new approach to the protection of a power transmission line based on transient phenomena following a fault inception. The main idea of the method is the use of a travelling wave line model which, by means of currents and voltages measured at one end of the transmission line, calculates the voltage distribution along the line. The algorithm consists of two main parts. One part is for the determination of the direction of a fault, and the second is the direct fault detection, which is independent of communication from the remote end protection. Verification of this method is carried out using digital simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of a directional comparison protection for EHV transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The need for improved power line protection has led to the development of a directional comparison protection based upon new operating principles. This new protection has a number of advantages over conventional line protection relays. The authors detail the operating principles of the protection, and consider the salient features of the new design. The operation of the protection is illustrated using the results of a study on a complex power system, where the fault waveforms are distorted by high frequency transients.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developments in transformer protection
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors describe a digital structure using CMOS plug-in modules to provide a versatile protection relay which can be programmed to match the wide range of applications for power system transformers. The microprocessor based digital technique has been exploited to provide a unit whose settings and characteristics are software controlled. The relay provides an extremely flexible three part operating characteristic with a range of variable bias slopes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A microprocessor protection relay for source protection of 11-kV radial distributors-its design and field trial experience
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors describe a scheme which provides for the protection of a 11 kV radial distribution feeder, the distribution transformers connected to the feeder, and provides a range of alarm functions and measurements. The relay will also record, cumulatively, interrupted current which may be of use in respect to the maintenance of the associated switchgear.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New approach to Teed feeder protection using composite current and voltage signal comparison
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The basis of a new approach to the problem of differential protection of Teed feeders that involves deriving differential signals which are functions of both voltages and currents measured at each feeder end are described. It is shown that this approach obviates the need for relay bias to compensate for capacitance spill current, improves the sensitivity to high resistance faults and removes uncertainties as to the dependability of protection under contingency operating and/or fault conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Extensive testing of algorithms for travelling-wave-based protection
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: To assure a continued supply of electricity, it is necessary to disconnect all short circuit situations as soon as possible. The author describes two algorithms for travelling wave-based power system protection, a technique which almost immediately recognises a fault on the network. Both algorithms use phase selection after fault detection and use a low-pass filter and a threshold to prevent false tripping.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interactive power system simulation for the laboratory evaluation of power system protection relays
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Attention has been focused on developing improved methods for evaluating the performance of modern protective relays, and in particular, relays used for EHV transmission line protection. The techniques described by the authors are based on digital power system simulation and extend the concepts of the programmable transmission line (PTL). In such a system, data generated by simulation programs is transformed into real-time current and voltage signals, which, after amplification provide the relay under test with input signals similar to those which it would encounter under fault conditions while in service. The authors describe the implementation of the PTL technique using a widely available desk-top microcomputer and the development of new features which enable the relay's response to both fault and post trip conditions to be examined. System operation is illustrated using tests which model the difficult operating conditions associated with a particularly onerous power system configuration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of ground protection of unit connected generators using third harmonics
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: On unit connected generators, ordinary zero sequence voltage relays used for stator winding protection against single phase ground fault can't cover 100% of the stator winding, i.e. there is a dead zone at or near the generator neutral. With the increase of generator capacity, especially the application of inner water cooling technology, ground protection for 100% stator winding is required. Protection based on response to third harmonic voltage can reliably cover the dead zone of zero sequence voltage protection and together with it constitutes the stator's 100% ground protection. Third harmonic ground protection can be realized in different ways. The authors deal with a protection scheme with additional compensation circuitry. It differs from the Kiskachi scheme in that amplitude and phase compensation circuitry are used so that the protection sensitivity is favorably improved. A comprehensive analysis of the scheme is made.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Differential line protection application to multi-terminal lines
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The study and development of differential line protection have been undertaken by ENERTEC PSC in particular to meet the requirements of the 1986 protection plan for the EDF 400 kV network. The author describes the principles chosen for the construction of the various protection elements and gives their results and performance levels in terms of operating features: detection sensitivity for resistive faults; and stability in the presence of faults external to the system being protected.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New accurate transmission line fault location equipment
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The use of longer distance transmission lines coupled with demands for reduced circuit outage times is stimulating a requirement for reliable and accurate fault location methods. The need for very high accuracy is generally becoming more important since, in EHV power systems, there is often little visual evidence of a fault, and post-fault clearance tests performed at reduced system voltage can be inconclusive. In this paper, the results of simulation studies to determine the basic accuracy of new fault location methods are given. The authors conclude with a description of the hardware implementation of the fault location equipment that is currently under development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accurate fault location of transmission lines using microprocessors
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The author presents an accurate algorithm to estimate the location of a transmission line fault. This method uses the fundamental frequency voltages and currents measured at the line terminals. These measurements are not required to be synchronized and the algorithm does not involve any simplifying assumptions. The algorithm is accurate since it solves the sequence network of the equivalent power system directly. The algorithm is evaluated using a 345 kV, 160 mile transmission line model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Research and application of protection relay schemes for internal faults in stator windings of a large hydro-generator with multi-branch and distributed arrangement
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Along with the development of the electric power industry, the protection for internal faults of large hydrogenerators with multi-branch and distributed neutral arrangements has become more and more important. The internal short-circuit current may be several times larger than the terminal short-circuit current inside the stator windings, and such strong current could cause severe heat and mechanical damage. The authors discuss various relay protection schemes for internal hydrogenerator faults. They briefly describe the multi-loop method for the analysis of such internal faults.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of an expert system for power system protection coordination
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The author describes the development of a prototype expert system for the protection coordination of an industrial power system. The system has proved successful to-date, however the knowledge base requires expansion to cover a larger portion of the application domain. Therefore, the reliability and integrity of the system are still to be tested. The graphic user interface can respond within nearly a second, even for redrawing a large power system map. On the other hand a computation and reasoning time is rather long. The protection coordination computation takes about 10 seconds for the previous example but each reasoning of answer takes about one minute to get a solution. The use of empirical rules results in a faster computation when heuristic search techniques can be used to integrate analytical techniques into an expert system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The performance of a protective scheme based on travelling waves
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: A selection of results are presented showing the ability of a protective algorithm to discriminate between internal and external power system faults. Particular emphasis is placed on complications created by the presence of modes of propagation in multiconductor systems such as double circuit lines. Some results of the effects of harmonics and noise are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of system control centre computer assisted special protection systems in Ontario Hydro
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors describe how transmission constraints caused by regulatory delays have been reduced by the use of special protection systems at Ontario Hydro's largest generation complex. The role of the system control centre computers in Ontario Hydro's evolving special protection system technology is described and the tradeoffs between risks and benefits associated with the use of special protection systems are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experience with a modern real-time power system simulator
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: ABB Relays has developed a digital, computer-controlled, electronic, analog power-system simulator. The simulator is used to evaluate new protection concepts in connection with product development work by its efficient real-time simulation capability, which enables parametric testing. Moreover, it is also utilized for the type testing of prototype protection equipment and verification for various customer applications. The power system simulator has undergone extensive testing by several utilities. A brief account of the operational experience with the simulator is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distance digital algorithm immune to saturation of current transformers
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Saturation of current transformers (CT) may introduce errors in operation of distance relays. To avoid the errors only the current phasors in the intervals should be calculated when the CT is unsaturated. The proposed algorithm calculates phasors of the current, utilizing algorithms with variable data window. The first results are obtained after the third sample of the fault current, so the calculation may be completed before the current transformer saturates. The algorithm is repeated in each cycle, during intervals of nonsaturation. The errors in calculation the amplitude of the primary current fundamental component is less than 10%, while the phase angle error is smaller than 4 deg., even if the current transformer is very severely saturated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive digital distance protection
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Since the state-of-the-art for microprocessors now allows for ever increasingly rapid calculation of results, the field of digital distance protection in power systems is now extending itself to include other power system contingency conditions. The authors extend this field of study by describing simulation studies performed in developing a digital distance relay which is capable of adapting itself to onerous power system conditions such as power swings and high-resistance earth faults. It is shown that the relay is capable of reliable and discriminative operation. The work has been computer simulated and attention has been paid to ensure that the simulation closely emulates the operation of prototype hardware under development. This includes a 16 bit microprocessor with the relay analogue measurands being digitised by a 14 bit A/D converter at a 4 kHz sample rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A microprocessor based protective system for generator-transformer units
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors describe a general concept of a digital protective system for large generator-transformer units. The main principle of this system is presented and some of its protective functions are discussed. Special attention is given to the overall impedance protective scheme which integrates all the tasks realised separately in conventional techniques by individual relays, i.e. back-up distance, loss of excitation and loss of synchronism (pole-slipping) protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Load shedding scheme of the Jordanian national power system
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Since 1977, underfrequency relays have been used in the Jordan Electricity Authority (JEA) power system to disconnect a predetermined portion of load when the frequency falls due to loss of generation. More recently rate-of-change frequency sensitive relays and undervoltage relays have been used to complete the load shedding scheme. The authors describe this load shedding scheme which aims at preventing a cascade trip of the system generating units and avoid a total system collapse.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of new protection for interconnected overhead 33 kV circuits
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: A new protection scheme has been developed for use on interconnected 33 kV circuits. This development was necessary principally because of the insecurity of existing metallic rented pilots. The project was undertaken in conjunction with a University which has a long established collaborative relationship with the utility concerned. A proprietary hardware relay product was used as the basis of the scheme and the software utilises substantial modules of established program which have been used in a variety of applications. The confidence level in the scheme as a whole is high because of the investment in both simulation testing and test bench testing. The equipment is connected to a live circuit and is permitted to operate circuit breakers in a trial installation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new digital technique for measuring frequency at a power system bus
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors present a new algorithm for estimating power system frequency from the voltage samples taken at pre-selected intervals of time. The method first calculates the phase angles of the phasor representing the voltage waveform and then estimates the frequency from the phase angles. The frequency changes are tracked by a feedback technique. A Kalman filter then removes noise from the frequency measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical fibre current sensor for circuit protection
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: An optical fibre current sensor has been designed and tested. This device, which uses the Faraday effect in optical fibre to measure electrical current, is intended to be applied to protection systems; it is regarded as a potential replacement for the iron cored current transformer in certain applications. The authors describe the design of an optical fibre current sensor, and review the considerations which led to the adoption of this particular design. Some background optical information is provided in order to make the design process clear, including outlines of the Faraday effect itself and of the major difficulty to be overcome; an effect known as linear birefringence. The results of current measurement tests on the optical fibre current sensor are presented and analysed in comparison with a current transformer. The advantages of the optical fibre current sensor for protection applications are summarized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprocessor based integrated feeder protection RIR 2000
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors present a microprocessor based integrated feeder protection with an autoreclosing function added to the protection scheme. The relay's design is based on 16-bit microprocessor with the corresponding 1/0 units for measuring analog and digital quantities. The digital processing of measured currents enables a separate setting of operating values, selection of all types of inverse or constant time characteristics for individual phases and earth fault. The microprocessor design enables automatic relay calibration, software and hardware self testing, and communication with the substation computer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Setting distance relays for multi-coupled lines using permissive under-reach schemes
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Environmental and financial pressures force electricity supply organizations to make maximum use of corridors available for transmission lines. This results in extensive use of double circuit lines and even several lines in close proximity. It is well known that zero sequence mutual coupling between such lines distorts the accuracy of distance relay measurements during earth faults. The setting of distance relays for lines that have multiple couplings and are terminated at different busbars, is a complex task. The authors detail some of the related problems and suggest a method for setting distance relays which form a permissive underreach scheme.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modern practices and field experience with MC-based relays
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: When the advantages of microcomputer (MC) technology in protective relaying are added to the communication facilities given by local and wide area networks (LANs and WANs), there are almost unlimited possibilities for the future development of protective and network management. It is expected that the bulk of protective equipment delivered in the future will go into conventionally designed plants and must, therefore, fit into the existing equipment in terms of constructive set-up, interfacing, environmental conditions and operating and testing policies. Power supply utilities which are faced with a new situation of low rate of energy demand growth must apply policies which concentrate investment more on that which is essential than that which is possible or desirable. Protection concepts with MC-based relays which correspond to the above outlined policy are discussed. The concepts are based on actual installations and on the recommendations of the Association of German Power Supply Authorities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical fibre signalling for protection purposes
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Modern digital signalling techniques now offer considerable improvements in power system protection signalling. By using optical fibre technology, distance protection and intertripping can be considerably improved in speed, reliability and security with simple, status and command mode signalling. The authors discuss an application of optical technology which provides a number of very fast and secure signalling commands over optical fibres associated with a 132 kV line and satisfying most requirements for signalling diversification or duplication.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Over and undervoltage protection of weakly interconnected HV long line networks
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors describe the voltage slide protection scheme is designed to maintain acceptable voltages to the majority of customers, who are situated electrically distant from a major generating pool, following multiple outage contingencies on the interconnecting transmission system. This is done by maintaining a reasonable reactive power balance in the load centre by switching in shunt capacitors and shedding portions of the load if necessary. If installed and set correctly this system should prevent a major brown-out or black-out of large portions of a power system, as has been the case in many large power system disturbances throughout the world.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Novel methods of protection and control equipment accommodation
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The CEGB 275/400 kV Supergrid System comprises 209 substations of varying age. In them there are 1668 feeder main protection units and 486 items of signalling equipment. Approximately 65% of these have an unsatisfactory performance, some other kind of limitation or are obsolete. Feeder protection alone provides the CEGB with approximately 25 circuits per year needing to be refurbished, which due to the time taken to carry out the work plus the increased rate of obsolescence of modern equipment, provides a perpetual workload unless times for design, draughting, installation, testing and commissioning of equipment can be considerably reduced. The author describes new techniques for accommodation of protection and control equipment at new and existing substations. The objective is to give reductions in lifetime costs and overall engineering time without loss and if possible, improvements in availability and reliability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved microprocessor based distribution feeder earth fault protection using pattern recognition
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: High impedance electrical faults usually occur when a high-voltage distribution line conductor is contacted by a high-impedance earthed object, such as a tree, or when a conductor breaks and falls on a poorly conducting earth surface. Such faults affect the quality of power supply and may present safety hazards. It is important to have a sensitive distribution feeder earth fault protection which is capable of detecting high-impedance faults accurately. The new relay proposed by the authors with the aid of modern technology and development in microprocessors, will be able to discriminate correctly between normal and high impedance fault conditions, due to its ability to continuously monitor system conditions. The authors briefly discuss high impedance faults, current and voltage patterns, arcing faults analysis and the microprocessor based distribution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simplification of polyphase line protection
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The term 'polyphase line protection' refers to a solid state line protection system in which the measuring units use sequence quantities. Such schemes are designated 'polyphase' since generally each measuring unit can respond to faults of a given type (e.g., phase-to-ground) on all phases or phase-pairs, and some measuring units can respond to different types of faults. Traditionally most GE solid state directional and distance measuring units have employed phase angle comparator circuits. This has been the basic approach used in solid distance relays from the early SLY/SLCG to the latest modular TLS relays. However, these units may also be implemented using an amplitude comparator as well as a phase angle comparator. The use of amplitude comparators is not entirely new in GE designs. They have been used for many years in the SLYP/SLYN and SLYP/SLCN polyphase relay schemes. The operating principles of phase and comparators and the existing amplitude comparators are reviewed followed by an introduction to the new features of the 'energy comparators' to be used in the polyphase line system relay system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A second generation microprocessor line protection relay
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors describe a line protection with distance relay and auxiliary functions, having an optimized hardware and software structure, for power transmission and sub-transmission as well as distribution applications. The development of this relay has evolved from an earlier prototype line protection equipment which was based on a single Intel 8086 16-bit microprocessor hardware and programmed in assembler language. The protection algorithms for the new line protection relay have thereby been thoroughly proven through many successful laboratory and field tests. The firmware and menu-driven man-machine interface (MMI) concepts are the same as for a new bus-oriented multi-processor generator protection system. Since the line and generator protection equipment share a common firmware concept, all available protection or measurement functions are compatible with both equipments. Through the use of continuous self-monitoring and self-testing, any hardware failures can be immediately reported, thereby reducing the probability of relay maloperation to virtually zero.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a generic range of distance relays
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The design of the described generic range of distance relays differs from most other new designs in that it uses multiprocessor hardware in an evolutionary way, making maximum use of the experience gained with earlier generations of distance relay. Microprocessors have been employed in the measuring circuits to produce a direct software equivalent of the hardware phase comparator used in earlier generations, having an operating principle which has been fully documented in previous literature. The principle uses analogue preconditioning and digital processing to achieve a fast operating time while preserving immunity from noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer generation of test quantities for testing protection relays
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Modern high-voltage power systems need secure high performance protection devices which have a high speed of operation for internal system fault conditions and a high level of discrimination between internal and external system faults. To achieve the high performance required by the power system, modern protection devices have, of necessity, become complex, electronic measuring systems employing large numbers of diverse types of electronic components. This increase in complexity along with the need to reduce the cost of maintenance has encouraged the development and use of automated protection test equipment. The author briefly describes an automatic protection test set which has been in use for a number of years in the UK, and describes how it has been further developed both to keep pace with developments in relaying and to satisfy users requirements for more flexible and cost effective equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System analysis of digital differential power transformer protection
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors present some findings relating to the design of digital differential transformer protection. They limit themselves to the key questions of digital filtering, phase compensation and harmonic restraint. They point out some solutions which can be implemented with success in the protection algorithm. They present a model of a power transformer which is equipped with an additional current transformer and thus enables simulation of the actual operating conditions and successful testing of protective algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new detection scheme for realisation of magnetising inrush current in transformers
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The computational model developed has been used to predict the pattern of magnetising inrush current for any combination of switching parameters in both single-phase and three-phase transformers. The pattern of second harmonic current during the inrush condition has been found to be inconsistent with the conventional second harmonic-restraint algorithm used in transformer differential relays. The reason is that the largest percentage second harmonic current may not necessarily appear in the first cycle but during any other of the initial few cycles. The new detection algorithm uses the real-time integration value of the magnetising inrush with a time span of one cycle. This method has been found to be consistent under any switching condition. Such a scheme can be readily tailored to replace the second harmonic tuned filter circuit used in the conventional second harmonic-restraint differential relay.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MORGAT: digital simulator used for industrial qualification of protective relays
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Electricite de France decided that a new tool needed to be developed for efficiency testing relays. The required tool had to accurately simulate a wide range of transient electric phenomena for a wide range of varied network topologies and be easy to use. To fulfil these requirements, a digital simulator, MORGAT, has been designed to reproduce transient electric phenomena. MORGAT basically consists of a program which computes electric system transients and of a real-time input/output facility delivering these transients to actual protection and control equipment. The system is made available using a sophisticated man-machine interface. Testing a protection is performed in two stages: first, the electric transients are computed then the results of computation are applied in real time to the tested relays, using an analog-to-digital converter associated with voltage and current amplifiers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive control of load shedding relays under generation loss conditions
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Two approaches to emergency load shedding have been evaluated by means of simulations of a representative system over a range of loads. The load shedding schemes examined were a conventional discrete frequency system, and an adaptive rate-of-change of frequency system. It was found that more accurate load shedding was achieved with the adaptive rate-of-change of frequency technique, the mismatch being 21%, compared with 37% for the discrete frequency scheme. The performance of the adaptive scheme was limited by a loss of discrimination in cases where the largest infeeds did not correspond to the most severe potential generation outages from the point of view of required load shedding. Further rationalization of load shedding requires a system-wide communications facility to identify the tripped generating unit, and instruct the appropriate relays to shed the minimum load in sufficient time to ensure frequency recovery.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic earth fault isolation and restoration of supply in cable distribution networks
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The author discusses the use of faulted section indicators (FSI) to reduce revenue losses after a cable fault on 11 kV carbon distribution networks. Following the detection of earth fault current, FSI transmit their location back along the 11/13 kV cable, using, time slotted, high frequency mains borne signals, to a receiver located in the primary substation. This receiver logs in the fault location data and interfaces with a telecontrol/SCADA system to enable onward transmission of the data to the central control room. The control engineer is thus able to give the precise location of the faulted section of cable together with instructions as to which switching operations must be performed to enable an engineer to go directly to the relevant secondary substations and re-configure the network with the minimum delay.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An assessment of the performance of distance and IDMT overcurrent relays for phase faults on interconnected power system networks
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: A computer program written in FORTRAN V has been developed for use in the assessment of the performance of inverse definite minimum time (IDMT) directional and nondirectional overcurrent relays, with or without high set elements, and distance mho relays or any combination of these. The algorithm can deal with multiple bulk supply points, parallel lines, parallel transformers, or three terminal lines (teed circuits). The algorithm allows for the creation of an island and can obtain the elements of the bus impedance matrix in the islanded and nonislanded parts which is not possible by direct matrix inversion or an ordinary outage procedure. The algorithm is applicable to three phase faults and has the capability to deal with all kinds of feeder configurations. Arrangements have been made to cover all parts of the feeder configurations as fault points.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution system protection-the application of modular electronic schemes
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The introduction of the modular distribution network protection schemes and philosophy has resulted in a dramatic increase in the number of Phase 2 schemes being applied throughout Eskom's South African distribution network. The schemes provide the necessary building blocks to implement a cost effective approach to the protection of the network, whilst accommodating the diverse requirements of the various regions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Overall assessment of distribution back up protection using microcomputer
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors introduce an interactive package using microcomputers with full graphic features to assess the performance of IDMT relays for overcurrent protection for distribution system with up to 35 substations and 50 lines in a ring, and a radial or interconnected system with several sources. It provides full range of colour graphic display of the single line of the whole or part of the distribution network and details of CT ratio, relay settings, simulated relay movement for all feeders in any selected substation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprocessor-based auto synchroniser for the CEGB's transmission system
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The Central Electricity Generating Board which presently owns and controls the 400 kV and 275 kV supergrid system in England and Wales operates a policy at both these voltages of delayed auto-reclosing (DAR) the switchgear equipment in conjunction with check synchronising. This is the procedure whereby a circuit breaker is closed across an already paralleled system. The equipment used for this purpose is provided on a per circuit basis. The Board also operates a policy of having system synchronisers at selected major substations for the purpose of recoupling a split system in the event of a system breakaway or island situation. These devices were installed on a one per substation basis and are switched into a circuit as required. The authors describe how after a review of this policy a new approach using microprocessors was adopted and a device was designed, evaluated and type approved to meet the new requirements and provide flexibility for possible future needs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A rationalised policy for application and setting of back-up protection on the CEGB supergrid system
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: There has been increasing pressure from system operators for back-up protection settings which allow unrestricted use of primary plant loading capability. Performance objectives and a setting policy for back-up protection have been developed. The setting policy provides an acceptable compromise between the conflicting requirements of protection sensitivity and system loading. It also seeks to minimise the engineering resources required for the determination of the settings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The management of the commissioning of the protection of Torness Power Station and substations
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Torness Power Station and the associated transmission system consists of a 132 kV double busbar substation, a 400 kV mesh substation and a nuclear power station with two advanced cooled reactors driving two 685 MW turbogenerators. The author provides an insight into the commissioning of protection for both the substations and power station. The author discusses the switchboards, station transformer, generator transformer, shunt reactor, and turbogenerator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System back-up protection-a new approach
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: In a high voltage transmission network, fast and discriminative main protection systems are essential on order to maintain the required power system stability. As complete reliability of any main protection system is not possible, failures of the protection systems or associated circuit breakers must also be considered. To safeguard against these failures, some form of back-up scheme is required to supplement the main protection system. Because of the conflicting 'speed' and 'discrimination' requirements, the back-up protection is seldom adopted on a system-wide basis in the transmission network. With the technological advancement in relays, more sophisticated static electronic relays are available and a better approach to provide the system back-up protection is therefore possible. The authors describes in detail the requirements and application techniques to achieve an effective system back-up protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Monitoring and fault protection of high voltage switchyards by the REMMIT method
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: A new method is described for the protection of HV switchyards which is based on the measurement of the magnetic field at a safe working distance from high voltage conductors. The theoretical framework for this method, called the 'REMMIT' (REmote Magnetic field Monitoring Instrument Transformer) system, is detailed and summarized. The authors outline the theoretical basis for the model and discuss experimental development to date.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Use of data compression techniques in digital fault recorder
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The purpose of the fault recorder is to pick up all events occurring on feeders to be monitored in substations. The fault recorder will then give the history of what happened before, during and after the fault. The authors describe the use of a digital fault recorder system which employs data compression techniques. Results obtained from such a system are also detailed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developments in distance protection
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The block average comparison principle for distance relay comparators has been successfully applied and well proven for many years. The only significant improvement to the basic scheme has been the introduction of a third signal S3 (I/sub L/ZR), to the comparator gate, which improved stability for feeder de-energisation and allowed the introduction of additional characteristics (e.g. directional shaped reactance, etc.). The author describes a method of decreasing the minimum comparator operating time by a factor of two and the practical benefits obtained due to the use of microprocessor technology in the control of a distance protection relay based on the block average comparison principle.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On site testing of protection and automatic switching equipment in 275 and 400 kV substations
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Protection performance is dependent on the availability of accurate and reliable protection relays and their connection to high quality measuring transformers and well designed tripping systems. But it is only in the substation that all elements of protection systems are brought together during site installation and hence can be tested for the first time. The author describes the re-examination of on site testing requirements and methods undertaken during CEGB reorganisation. He shows that the introduction of new technology and increasing system utilisation factor has been fully taken into account.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design aspects of Torness main generator protection
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The South of Scotland Electricity Board's new power station at Torness consists of two 685 megawatt turbine generators driven by steam from reactors of the Advanced Gas Cooled design. The first generator was commissioned in May 1988 and the author describes the protection design philosophy applied to the main generator and associated plant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer controlled protection testing-a Western Australian experience
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: Accurate secondary injection testing of power system protection equipment is essential in order to establish performance characteristics both in the laboratory and in the field. Traditional, analogue test equipment has not always provided the desired results. This is because analogue equipment that will produce these results is very complex, cumbersome and expensive. The availability of powerful, compact computers and microchip technology have provided the means to take an innovative approach to this problem. The author describes a project which was initiated by the protection section of SECWA to exploit this technology to provide both a laboratory test facility and a portable equipment suitable for use in the field.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aspects of modern secondary relay testing equipment
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors briefly discuss the reasons for testing power system protection relays and then describe the RP86 test system. The system is based on a personal computer. The amplifiers and control units are described and the three modes of operation, menu operated, program operated and graphic modes, are explained. The equipment provides economic testing combined with high precision of measured values.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprocessor motor protection relay
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The authors describe the IMM 7990 relay for HV asynchronous motor protection. Various functions provided by the relay are briefly described including thermal overload protection, starting protection, and faults protection. The operation of the relay and the options available are also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Expert system applications in substation monitoring, back-up protection and control
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: As microelectronic technology spreads into the field of substation automation, an integrated protection and control system is developed and discussed by the authors. An expert system has been built to meet the functional demands of a substation, in an integrated protection and control system concept. The simulation tests of this project were performed on IBM personal computers and correct results were obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Industrial feeder protection
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The successful application of protective relays depends upon three factors, namely: initiating action to isolate the faulty part(s) of the electrical power namely: initiating action to isolate the faulty part(s) of the electrical power system; limiting the effects of fault(s) to an acceptable level on the healthy parts of the system; and accomplishing this at an acceptable cost. The authors concentrate upon meeting the foregoing objectives on power system feeders supplying industrial loads. In particular the techniques discussed relate to the necessity to maintain the security of essential loads, where the stability of rotating machinery is a vital consideration. There is an increasing need for higher speed clearance of faults on systems to which electrically-controlled motor drives are connected. Means for the post-fault restoration of supplies to loads which have been disconnected due to faults are also considered. In this respect the advantages of telesignalling via the distribution feeders in order to accelerate the isolation of the faulty section are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of an integrated protection and reclosing relay for rural feeders
publicationTitle: 1989 Fourth International Conference on Developments in Power Protection
abstract: The problems encountered in South African 11 kV rural power lines due to the nature of African electric storms is discussed by the author. The relay developed to overcome the problems (type GAD) offers two overcurrent inputs each of which incorporates low set and high set instantaneous elements for instantaneous tripping as well as IDMTL tripping, switch selectable to normal inverse, very inverse, extremely inverse and definite time lag. A separate earth fault input offers similar features to the overcurrent inputs. In addition, a sensitive earth fault element is provided. The author describes the features of this reclosing relay including: definite time on instantaneous elements; line check, status input sensitive earth fault, and busbar zone protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
